 Darius Acuff Jr., Malik Monk, Keegan Murray, Dylan Cardwell and Domantas Sabonis will start Sunday’s game against the Thunder. 
 The Kings are without Zach LaVine and De’Andre Hunter, opening up two spots in the starting lineup. Monk and Cardwell will fill the resulting voids, making both players worth streaming in deep leagues.

 Malik Monk 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Malik Monk amassed 14 points (6-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine (illness) is out for Sunday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Absent from the initial injury report, LaVine is now out for Sunday’s game. With De’Andre Hunter questionable and Precious Achiuwa out, the Kings could be extremely shorthanded. Malik Monk and Emanuel Sharp should see their minutes increase with LaVine out. 
 Maxime Raynaud 
 SAC 
 Center 
 #42 
 Kings insider James Ham reports that Maxime Raynaud (knee) is progressing but has no official timeline to return. 
 The backup big man has yet to make his season debut, but until he returns, Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa should continue to pickup the slack in the frontcourt. 
 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa (leg) finished Tuesday’s loss to the Magic with 10 points (3-of-6 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and one three-pointer. 
 Achiuwa had to leave Tuesday’s game with just under eight minutes left in the third quarter with a leg contusion and did not return. His early exit gave Dylan Cardwell (1/12/1/2/2) more playing time, and he logged 29 minutes off the bench. Keegan Murray (11/2/1 with four blocks and two three-pointers) played 24 minutes as he continues to work his way back from an ankle injury. 
 Maxime Raynaud 
 SAC 
 Center 
 #42 
 Maxime Raynaud (knee) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Magic. 
 Working his way back from a right patellar subluxation suffered during the preseason, Raynaud was to be re-evaluated early this week. That did not happen on Monday, but the Kings are listing the second-year center out for Tuesday night. Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell have been providing depth at center when Domantas Sabonis is not on the floor. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine recorded 15 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Heat. 
 LaVine shot the ball well on Sunday, but the playing time was an eye-opener. He played 25 minutes against the Heat and did not return after being subbed out with 4:03 remaining in the third quarter. The Kings made no injury announcement, and LaVine was called for one foul, so foul trouble couldn’t have been the reason. Kings head coach Doug Christie played Darius Acuff Jr. and Malik Monk (9/2/3/1) in the backcourt for the entire fourth quarter, which left no room for LaVine. That’s something for fantasy managers to watch moving forward. 
 Dylan Cardwell 
 SAC 
 Center 
 #32 
 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell will start Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 The Kings are without Domantas Sabonis (knee) for Sunday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. Cardwell will replace him, and the Kings will need his rebounding and defense. Also, Hunter reclaims his place in the lineup with Leaky Black heading to the bench. And Achiuwa remains in the starting lineup despite Keegan Murray returning from an ankle injury. 
 Domantas Sabonis 
 SAC 
 Forward-Center 
 #11 
 Domantas Sabonis (knee) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 Sabonis is a late addition to the Kings’ injury report due to a sore left knee. If he can’t play against the Heat, the Kings will have to rely more on Dylan Cardwell in the post. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter (illness) is out for Friday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Hunter’s absence opens up a spot in the Kings’ starting lineup. Malik Monk and Leaky Black may see their minutes increase, whether or not they join the starting lineup. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter (illness) is questionable for Friday’s matchup with the Spurs. 
 With Keegan Murray (ankle) still on the shelf, Sacramento’s rotation is already thin. If Hunter is forced to sit out against San Antonio, Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk could handle additional minutes.

 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) notched 14 points (6-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 After missing two games with a sprained ankle, Mitchell played 27 minutes against the Kings. The final stat line was solid, with the third-year guard doing everything but blocking a shot. Oklahoma City’s many injuries have put Mitchell in a position where he needs to be rostered in most leagues. And his skill set is such that maintaining top-100 value may not be too challenging. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Recap 
 More Ajay Mitchell News
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Sunday’s win over the Kings with 37 points (13-of-20 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers.
 In his final game of Week 4, Gilgeous-Alexander did whatever he wanted against the Kings. While shooting 65 percent from the field, the two-time MVP did not turn the ball over at all in 30 minutes of action. Oklahoma City’s blowout win meant Gilgeous-Alexander got some additional rest, as he did not play in the fourth quarter. SGA and the Thunder don’t play the first of their three Week 5 games until Wednesday. That isn’t great for fantasy managers, but it’s good for a team that’s been hit hard by injuries this season. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker 
 ATL

 Nickeil Alexander-Walker delivered 20 points (7-of-15 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 33 minutes to lead the Hawks to a 113-106 win over the Bucks on Sunday.
 Alexander-Walker has been an extremely consistent scoring threat, eclipsing 20 points on nine occasions this season. He’s offered a little bit of everything from a production standpoint, which has helped him grade out as an early-round fantasy contributor, averaging 21.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.5 steals and 0.4 blocks through 14 games. The Hawks are back in action with a three-game week that features tilts against the Thunder, Hornets and Pistons.
 -  George Bissell

 Kasparas Jakučionis 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Player Stats

 Kasparas Jakučionis tallied a career-high 25 points (9-of-16 FGs, 4-of-10 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and three steals in 26 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Hawks.
 Jakučionis took advantage of his opportunity with Ryan Rollins out with an illness, hoisting a season-high 16 shot attempts and going 4-of-10 from three-point range. He’s played sparingly in his Bucks debut, but he’s shown that he can heat up and score in bunches when he’s given a chance. His role figures to expand once the Bucks begin to jettison some of their veteran pieces around midseason. Milwaukee has a three-game week on tap with matchups against the Heat, Trail Blazers and 76ers.
 -  George Bissell

 CJ McCollum notched 20 points (5-of-10 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and four steals over 30 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Bucks.
 McCollum stepped back into Atlanta’s starting lineup with dynamic rookie Kingston Flemings sitting out with a back strain. The elder statesman saved his best for crunch time, scoring eight of his 20 points in the final four minutes, including going a perfect 4-for-4 at the line during that span, helping the Hawks seal a narrow victory. The Hawks have a three-game week coming up with showdowns against the Thunder, Hornets and Pistons.
